messages.author: 6f81c58ba9ed02c3
messages.subject: fiml vs fiml.x
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering if someone might be able to provide a basic description of when it would be appropriate to use fiml.x vs fiml for missing data (assuming already that the missing mechanism is MCAR or MAR). Also, is anyone aware of any literature that talks about how the fiml.x function works and its validity/utility for data analysis?

Thank you,

Ryan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: fiml vs fiml.x
parts:
fiml.x is just FIML that allows missing data on the exogenous predictors when fixed.x=TRUE.  I'm unsure about the practical implications.  If the sample statistics of the incomplete exogenous variables have to be estimated, then I would think that means they are no longer being treated as fixed, in which case I would just set fixed.x=FALSE to begin with.  

Frankly, I think the whole fixed.x=TRUE situations seems incredibly dubious to begin with in most SEM applications.  Are those values really determined by the study design?  Will they really remain the same from sample to sample gathered using the same method?

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
